[Checkmate3023] i feel like the Korean cars mainly KIA had a lot of success with their 7-year warrenty which was market leading for a long time - i still member many brands only offering 3 and some 5 year warrenties when Kia came in they blew away a lot of brands as they were priced below competition but to maintain faith they had a 'quality' 7 year warrenty.
now 5 and 7 is pretty stand but at the time Kia has the inside track i even remember a being in the states and chating to my Uber driver and he said he brought the Kia we were in just because of the warrenty
I do feel like MG are 'trying' to replicate that a bit with the 10 year warrenty but i dont know if it has been 'as' successful due to the sheer flood of cheap cars into the market - i actually feel like the value end is saturated but the 'luxury' end could use a bit of a shake up

[Checkmate3023] VW completely priced themselves out of the market
it might be part of the wider strategy as
I dont disagree they are on the piss with some of the VW pricing but the brand in is part of a Multi tier system globally and in Australia looking at buyers from all ends of the value chain Skoda being their budget option, VW for slight more Premium buyers and Audi/Cupra being their Mid-tier-Luxury end, and Premium Luxury Porsche the Ultra high Luxury / Niche end in Lambos/Bentley
Not to mention their commerical Vans - ie Caddy
if you want a 'Euro' car they essentially are open to all level of buyers - this also gives them a 'network' of service departments, sales teams, HR, parts etc
unlike other companies they are less reliant on collaborating with competition (although im sure the Amarok is made in the Ford Factories in Asia) - i actually think VW do a 'decent' job of running multiple brands for different buyers.
I compare them to the 'shit show' that is Stellantis which i wouldnt touch a car they have in their arsenal as they are over priced garbage many competing for the same buyers in many cases and their 'value cars' where all shit ie Fiat and Citeron
